items: Axiom Forge Mk1 / RECA research benchmark repository.
Studies Recursive Environment-Coupled Adaptation and future viability under recursively changing adaptation.
README definitions of recursive depth, consequence coupling, adaptive consolidation and future/generative viability.
Recursive depth alone is insufficient; consequence coupling and consolidation are proposed as necessary contributors to future viability.
Immediate performance vs long-horizon viability; ordinary adaptation vs structural/recursive mechanism modification.
Baseline-versus-RECA, perturbation and long-horizon benchmark design.
Proof-of-concept benchmark/research scaffold rather than completed empirical validation.
RECA should remain falsifiable by perturbation/future-viability evidence rather than terminology.
Causal/scale/estimator semantics of the multiplicative relation and future-viability construct remain unresolved.
Default YAML config specifies reca_vs_baseline, seed 42, 1000 steps, 10x10 goal environment, agent hyperparameters and results/raw/summary output settings.
Current performance can rise while consequence authority over future adaptation mechanisms is lost.
Theory definition of RECA plus D_c, C_e, A_c and G_V.
D_c*C_e*A_c -> G_V as a compact causal hypothesis, not a demonstrated law.
Fixed optimization, ordinary adaptive learning, recursive self-modification and consequence-coupled recursive adaptation are distinct regimes.
RECA predicts better recovery/future viability when structural changes remain consequence-coupled and consolidated.
Theory falsification requires testing whether RECA variables add predictive/explanatory value beyond simpler adaptation/performance variables.
Theory is framed as a testable benchmark hypothesis requiring validation.
Construct scales and causal identification for D_c,C_e,A_c,G_V remain unresolved.
Recursive depth should track modification depth; grounded changes require consequence contribution; useful changes should persist.
Baseline/ablation/full-RECA architecture supports isolating depth, coupling and consolidation.
Mechanism-level identity and future-viability horizon/estimation remain unresolved in the architecture spec.
Benchmark environment should expose consequence, perturbation/regime change, recovery and non-stationarity.
Controlled perturbation, long-horizon persistence and matched-resource comparison protocol.
Consequence-coupled recursive agents should recover better under relevant perturbation than fixed/non-coupled comparators.
Concrete perturbation distributions, recovery thresholds and statistical decision rules remain open.
Metric roles for recursive depth, consequence coupling, adaptive consolidation and future/generative viability.
Composite RECA score/result combines D_c,C_e,A_c as candidate predictors of G_V.
Shuffle/ablation/depth sanity checks plus repeated seeds, effect sizes/uncertainty and future-viability prediction doctrine.
Construct validity and absent executed inferential evidence remain unresolved.
Tests whether recursive/coupled/consolidated adaptation predicts future viability beyond baseline performance.
Baseline/RECA/ablation conditions, perturbation phases, outcome measures, repeated-seed inference and falsification controls.
High proxy score is insufficient without additional predictive/explanatory value for later viability.
Frozen implementation is not established by the specification as satisfying all benchmark conditions.
RECA implementation plan / definition of done.
Current code is treated as benchmark scaffold; stronger empirical completion criteria remain future work.
Definition of done calls for about 30+ seeds, effect-size/uncertainty reporting, ablations and structural metrics predictive of later viability.
Implementation priorities: runnable benchmark, metric wiring, perturbation, trace persistence, analysis and report generation.
Code/runnability completeness is distinct from evidence sufficient for the scientific claim.
No frozen result demonstrates the definition-of-done conditions.
Root executable imports and calls `run_experiment` from the reca_vs_baseline experiment module.
